subject: Re: MAP & sample provisioning — evaluation dataset exchange and close playbook
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael@polarisai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Briggs <evan@polarisai.com>
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval dataset & MAP — next steps

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — really liked the latency/readiness profile you showed. Polaris is ready to move forward with a short evaluation, but legal wants a clear mutual action plan and restrictions on dataset use before we ship our internal testcases.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you share a short MAP that outlines milestones + acceptance criteria and a recommended close timeline?
- We plan to push a 1200-sample prompt/testcase pack (sanitized). Need to confirm usage constraints (retention window, destruction, no redistribution) and whether Redwood will run the corpus in a dedicated customer sandbox or on hosted nodes.

Attached is a first-cut package of testcases. They are pseudonymized but include some sensitive PII patterns — legal will likely ask for a DS or a limited-access sandbox.

Attachments: polaris_testcases_v1.zip (zip, ~36MB)

Happy to hop on a 30min call this week to lock the timeline.

Best,
Michael
Sr. ML Engineer, PolarisAI
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael@polarisai.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval dataset & MAP — next steps

Michael — thanks, and great to hear you liked the demo.

I reviewed the package you attached. Next steps I propose (high level MAP + timeline):

1) NDA & narrow DPA amendment (this week) — both sides sign; Polaris legal shares redlines if any.
2) Secure dataset handoff (Week 2) — Polaris uploads to our restricted intake bucket; Redwood ingests into a customer-isolated sandbox (VPC) for the eval.
3) Trial configuration (Week 2–3) — we apply a Read-only KV prefix cache, session isolation, and restricted logs retention (90 days) per MAP.
4) Evaluation window (2 weeks) — customer runs testcases + Redwood runs identical baseline to collect metrics.
5) Acceptance review & close (Week 6) — mutual review of throughput/latency/quality metrics; signoff or next steps for Dedicated.

I attached a concise MAP and suggested acceptance criteria (latency P95 target, token cost per sample budget, accuracy tolerances). The MAP also contains the usage constraints we typically require: evaluation-only license, 90-day retention, no redistribution, and mandatory shredding of the raw testcases after the retention window unless you request extended retention in writing.

Two quick clarifications we need from you:
- Do you require us to run in your VPC (private deployment) or is the Redwood isolated sandbox acceptable?
- Any mandatory telemetry or logging requirements from legal/security at Polaris we should pre-authorize?

Attachments: Redwood_Eval_MAP_v1.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

If that looks good I can get legal and solutions engineering involved and we can schedule a document review call Wednesday 10am PT.

Thanks — look forward to closing this fast.

— Soojin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Briggs <evan@polarisai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Michael Torres <michael@polarisai.com>
Cc: legal@polarisai.com
Date: Wed, 4 May 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval dataset & MAP — next steps

On Wed, May 3, 2027 at 9:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Two quick clarifications we need from you:
> - Do you require us to run in your VPC (private deployment) or is the Redwood isolated sandbox acceptable?
> - Any mandatory telemetry or logging requirements from legal/security at Polaris we should pre-authorize?

Hi Soojin — thanks. Short answers:
- Preferred: Redwood sandbox is OK for this short eval as long as access is restricted to 3 Polaris engineers and logs are not retained beyond 90 days. If later we expand scope, we may ask for private deployment.
- Polaris legal requires an export-control clause plus a signed evidence of data handling for PII patterns (they won't share cleartext PII). We'll push redlines on the NDA and a short DPA addendum.

I'll be on the call Wed 10am PT with Michael and our legal counsel (cc'd).

Evan
Product Lead, PolarisAI
From: legal@polarisai.com <legal@polarisai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Michael Torres <michael@polarisai.com>, Evan Briggs <evan@polarisai.com>
Date: Thu, 5 May 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris — redlines for evaluation NDA 

Hi Soojin,

Attached are redlines to your standard NDA and a short DPA addendum focused on retention, logging, and export-control language. Main points:
- Add explicit 90-day retention cap and a contractual obligation to securely destroy ingested testcases on or before that date.
- Limit access to named Polaris engineers (Michael, Evan, and one SRE) and require access logs for any exceptions.
- Add export-control warranty and an indemnity carveout for exported model artifacts if Redwood exports copies to jurisdictions outside the US.

We included inline comments and a DocuSign-ready copy. Please review and confirm if Redwood can accept these redlines or propose alternate language.

Attachments: redlines_polaris_nondisclosure.docx (docx, 18KB)

Regards,
Polaris Legal Team
legal@polarisai.com
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: legal@polarisai.com, Michael Torres <michael@polarisai.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris — redlines for evaluation NDA 

Thanks for the redlines — appreciate the clarity. A couple of notes from Redwood ops/legal perspective:

- 90-day retention and destruct window: acceptable. We will implement a signed destruction ticket that both parties acknowledge; Redwood will provide a deletion certificate once the retention window ends.
- Named engineers access: we can restrict access to the 3 named Polaris engineers plus one Redwood SRE on a need-only basis. Access will be RBAC-limited and logged.
- Export-control language: we are comfortable with a mutual warranty that Redwood will not export raw Polaris testcases outside of US regions without written permission; however, we cannot accept indemnity carveouts tied to model parameter leakage — we propose a limited indemnity that excludes model architecture and pre-existing public data.

Next steps I recommend to keep the close timeline tight:
- Today/Tomorrow: sign NDA (DocuSign link) — Polaris legal to approve or accept our counter.
- Wednesday (Week 2): secure upload to restricted intake + ingestion validation by Redwood SRE.
- Week 2–4: 2-week eval window + metric collection; Redwood provides baseline runs and a token-cost estimate.
- Week 5: joint review; week 6: final decision/contracting.

I've added Rishi (security) to validate the sandbox configuration; Lauren (manager) to oversee the commercial close if the eval metrics meet the MAP. If you sign the DocuSign copy by EOD tomorrow we can hit the Week 2 upload as planned.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/PLS-4392/redwood-pol-nda (provisional link)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-eval-exchange

Best,
— Soojin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
